Energy | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Energy Affordable, reliable energy is essential to America’s economic strength, national security, and quality of life. Energy costs affect nearly every part of a family’s budget and every product a business makes or transports. Producing more energy here at home creates good-paying American jobs, lowers costs for families and businesses, and reduces our dependence on foreign adversaries. I support an all-of-the-above energy strategy that includes oil, natural gas, nuclear power, hydropower, wind, solar, carbon capture, and emerging energy technologies. America should responsibly develop its onshore and offshore resources while continuing to invest in innovation that makes energy production cleaner, safer, and more efficient. We can protect our air, water, and natural resources without sacrificing jobs, affordability, reliability, or national security. Virginia is well positioned to lead America’s next generation of energy production, particularly in nuclear fission and fusion technology. Nuclear power provides reliable, around-the-clock, carbon-free electricity and must be a central part of meeting our growing energy needs. I support modernizing outdated regulations, strengthening the domestic nuclear supply chain, and accelerating the development and deployment of advanced nuclear technologies, such as fusion. Producing additional energy is only part of the solution. America must also modernize its electric grid, pipelines, transmission systems, and other critical infrastructure so energy can reach the homes, military installations, and businesses that need it. Lengthy and unpredictable permitting processes delay energy projects, discourage investment, and ultimately increase costs for consumers. Permitting reform should establish reasonable timelines, improve coordination among federal agencies, and allow projects to move forward responsibly while maintaining appropriate environmental safeguards. Energy security also depends on access to critical minerals used in power generation, batteries, semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and nearly every modern defense system.

Seniors | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Seniors Social Security and Medicare are a promise we have made to hardworking Americans—and it is one I fully intend to keep. These programs are earned benefits tied to a lifetime of work, and seniors deserve peace of mind knowing that the benefits they count on will be there when they need them. Let me be clear: I will not support changes that reduce benefits for current beneficiaries or Americans nearing retirement. At the same time, we cannot ignore the serious long-term financial challenges facing Social Security and Medicare. Failing to act could result in automatic benefit reductions that would be devastating for millions of seniors. Congress must work across the aisle to strengthen these programs, eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse, and ensure their long-term sustainability for future generations. Protecting seniors also means ensuring access to affordable, high-quality health care. I am working to lower prescription drug costs, reduce unnecessary Medicare red tape, protect access to local health care providers, improve accountability in nursing homes, and help seniors recognize scams and safeguard their personal information. I also support policies that help Americans save for retirement throughout their working lives. By making it easier for small businesses to offer retirement plans and giving workers greater flexibility to build and manage their savings, we can help more Americans enter retirement with financial security and independence. For constituents navigating Social Security or Medicare, my office takes pride in providing first-class casework assistance. If you are experiencing a delay or difficulty with a federal benefit, my team stands ready to help. Veterans | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Veterans Virginia’s First District is home to thousands of veterans, and nearly 700,000 veterans call the Commonwealth home. Our veterans earned their benefits through sacrifice, service, and hardship, and they deserve our unwavering support. That means access to high-quality health care, timely delivery of benefits, educational and employment opportunities, and the resources necessary to successfully transition to civilian life. Veterans should not have to fight through unnecessary bureaucracy to receive the care and benefits they have earned. I am working to streamline the disability-claims process, improve information sharing between the Department of War and the Department of Veterans Affairs, expand access to appropriate community care, and hold the VA accountable for the quality and timeliness of its services. We must also confront veteran suicide and substance abuse with urgency. I support expanding access to mental health care, connecting veterans with counseling and crisis resources, identifying which suicide-prevention programs are most effective, and ensuring that veterans’ privacy is protected throughout the process. I formed the First District Veterans Advisory Board to hear directly from veterans about the challenges they face. Through the advisory board, veterans seminars, and meetings across the district, I will continue working with veterans, their families, veterans service organizations, and community leaders to improve the services available to those who served. My office also stands ready to assist veterans experiencing delays or difficulties with VA health care, disability claims, military records, or other federal benefits. Legislative Work Veterans Collaboration Act (H.R. 552) — Would establish a VA pilot program encouraging partnerships between veterans service organizations and law schools that provide veterans with assistance filing disability claims and appeals and addressing other legal needs. Broadband | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Broadband Reliable, affordable, high-speed internet is essential infrastructure for families, students, health care providers, farmers, and businesses. Yet many rural communities still lack the dependable service they need to access telehealth, pursue an education, work remotely, operate a business, or participate fully in today’s economy. For me, the issue of rural broadband dates back more than 20 years to my service on the Westmoreland County Board of Supervisors. As co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Rural Broadband Caucus and through the First District Broadband Task Force, I have consistently worked to expand reliable internet access across rural Virginia. Accurate broadband maps are essential to determining which communities remain unserved and ensuring federal resources reach the people who truly need them. I supported the Broadband DATA Act, which requires more precise, location-based reporting from internet service providers to improve the Federal Communications Commission’s National Broadband Map. Better data helps prevent duplicative spending, reduces overbuilding in communities that already have service, and holds providers accountable for the coverage they report. My Serving Rural America Act helped provide the model for the National Telecommunications and Information Administration’s Broadband Infrastructure Program. That $288 million program supports partnerships among states, localities, and broadband providers to deploy infrastructure in communities lacking reliable internet service. Public-private partnerships are especially important in rural communities, where the cost of building broadband infrastructure can exceed the revenue a provider can reasonably expect to earn. Virginia’s Telecommunications Initiative has demonstrated how localities, the Commonwealth, and private providers can work together to extend service into communities where the business case for private investment alone may not exist. Education | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Education My mother spent her career as a public school teacher in Hanover County, and my wife, Kathryn, devoted more than 40 years to teaching elementary school students in Westmoreland County. I have seen firsthand the early mornings, late evenings, and countless hours educators devote to helping students discover confidence in themselves and excitement for learning. Their dedication has a lasting impact on our children, families, and communities. Every student deserves access to a high-quality education and the opportunity to pursue a path that matches his or her talents and goals. Parents should never feel powerless when it comes to their children’s education. They deserve transparency about what their children are learning and a meaningful voice in the decisions that affect them. Education decisions should be made as close to students as possible, with parents, teachers, administrators, school boards, and local communities empowered to help children succeed. Strengthening America’s education system is also essential to maintaining our economic competitiveness and preparing the next generation for a rapidly changing workforce. That means supporting Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math (STEM) programs; expanding Career and Technical Education (CTE); increasing access to dual-enrollment courses; and strengthening partnerships among schools, community colleges, and local employers. These partnerships allow students to begin earning credentials while still in high school and help ensure education and training programs reflect the needs of the communities they serve. I supported the Strengthening Career and Technical Education for the 21st Century Act, which was signed into law. This legislation expanded access to CTE programs, strengthened partnerships between schools and the business community, modernized career training programs, and gave states and localities greater flexibility over how federal CTE resources are used. Health Care | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Health Care Before serving in Congress, I earned my master’s degree in public health and spent more than 26 years working for the Virginia Department of Health. That experience taught me that health policy works best when it puts patients, providers, and local communities first. Too many Virginians are paying more for health care while options for that care continue to shrink. Insurance companies delay or deny treatment, prescription drug middlemen contribute to higher costs, and patients often do not know what a procedure or medication will cost until the bill arrives. Health care should provide peace of mind—not surprise denials, hidden costs, or endless paperwork. I am working to build a health care system that protects individuals with pre-existing conditions, preserves access for vulnerable Americans, and gives families greater control over their health care options and dollars. Medical decisions should be made by patients and their doctors—not insurance company executives. Lowering health care costs requires greater transparency and competition. Patients should be able to understand their coverage, compare prices, and know what they will pay before receiving care. I support holding hospitals and insurers accountable for transparent pricing, making lower-cost generic and biosimilar medicines more readily available, and modernizing Health Savings Accounts so families have greater flexibility in managing their health care expenses. I am also working to hold insurance companies and Pharmacy Benefit Managers accountable. Patients deserve to know how frequently insurers deny claims, how long appeals take, and how many denials are ultimately overturned. Prescription drug discounts and rebates should benefit patients—not be absorbed by middlemen operating behind the scenes. I supported significant federal PBM reforms enacted in 2026 to increase transparency, reform hidden compensation practices, and protect access to independent pharmacies. Jobs & Economy | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Jobs & Economy A strong economy should allow families to afford their everyday needs, workers to keep more of what they earn, small businesses to grow, and every American to pursue a secure and successful future. Economic growth is not simply a statistic—it determines whether a paycheck goes far enough, whether a business can afford to hire another employee, or whether young people can find good employment opportunities close to home. The federal government’s role should be to eliminate barriers to success, not create them. That means supporting working families, maintaining a competitive tax code, producing affordable American energy, modernizing permitting, and removing unnecessary regulations that increase costs and prevent businesses from expanding. I supported the Working Families Tax Cuts to provide greater certainty and relief for families, workers, and small businesses. The law expanded family tax relief, provided tax relief for qualifying tips and overtime, strengthened incentives for American investment, and preserved important tax provisions for small businesses. Families and entrepreneurs should be able to plan for the future without facing constantly changing tax rules or sudden tax increases. Small businesses are the backbone of Virginia’s communities. They create jobs, support local organizations, and give our towns and neighborhoods their distinct character. I will continue working to ensure small businesses have access to capital, a trained workforce, a predictable regulatory environment, and a tax system that allows them to compete, invest, and grow. Workforce development is also essential to long-term economic growth. Employers across Virginia need skilled workers in health care, construction, manufacturing, transportation, shipbuilding, information technology, and other critical industries. We must expand Career and Technical Education, STEM programs, apprenticeships, dual-enrollment courses, and industry-recognized credentialing programs that connect students and workers with available jobs. Family Values | Congressman Rob Wittman Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Family Values A lot of people say they would not be where they are today without their parents. For me, that is the absolute truth. When I was eight months old, my mom and dad adopted me from the Children’s Home Society of Virginia in Richmond. My birth mother made the selfless decision to give me opportunities she felt unable to provide, and my parents’ decision to adopt changed the course of my life. That experience instilled in me a lasting commitment to protecting the most vulnerable among us and supporting families as they form, grow, and care for one another. Every child deserves a safe, stable, and loving home, and parents should have the resources and support they need to build strong families. Adoption can be an extraordinary expression of love, but expectant parents cannot consider an option they do not know is available. That is why I authored the Adoption Information Act, which would ensure expectant parents receiving federally supported family-planning services have access to information about adoption. I have also fought to protect and expand the Adoption Tax Credit and reduce the financial barriers faced by families that open their homes to children through adoption. As a child of adoption, I understand the extraordinary lengths people will go to become parents. I strongly support continued access to in vitro fertilization (IVF) and other treatments that help families experiencing infertility have children..
